questions.q: What happens when ten users open a report configured to "Always run with the most recent data"?
options: Only the first user's request queries the data source; the rest are cached
The report refuses to open for more than one user at a time
Ten separate queries are sent to the data source, one per user
The report runs once on a schedule regardless of how many users open it
questions.explain: On-demand execution queries the data source fresh every time — the most accurate option, but also the most expensive under concurrent load.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a cached copy and a report snapshot?
options: There is no real difference — they're two names for the same feature
A snapshot can only be created manually, never on a schedule
A cached copy is created opportunistically when a user requests the report; a snapshot is captured deliberately on a schedule, independent of anyone viewing it
A cached copy stores only the data, while a snapshot stores only the layout
questions.explain: Caching reacts to a user's request; a snapshot runs on its own schedule and is stored in the report server database whether or not anyone opens the report.

questions.q: Which type of report can NOT be cached or run as a snapshot?
options: A report that uses a shared data source instead of an embedded one
A report that includes a chart or gauge
A report that prompts for user credentials or uses Windows-integrated security to reach its data source
A report that has more than one dataset
questions.explain: Reports whose correct output depends on who's viewing them, or that rely on per-user Windows-integrated security, have no single safe copy to cache or snapshot.

questions.q: Why does a snapshot require a default parameter value for a parameterized report?
options: Because SSRS requires all snapshots to use exactly zero parameters
Because parameters are disabled entirely once a report is snapshotted
Because a snapshot locks in one specific data pull at creation time, and there's no user present to supply a parameter interactively
Because the default value is only used for display, not for the actual query
questions.explain: A snapshot runs on a schedule with no user interacting with it, so it needs a default parameter value to know what data to pull.

questions.q: Which report gets the most real benefit from caching?
options: A report that's never actually opened by anyone
A report whose output is different for every single viewer
A daily sales dashboard the whole team opens every morning
A report exactly one person checks once a month
questions.explain: Caching pays off when a shared, frequently-viewed report is requested often enough that reusing a rendered copy beats re-running the query each time.
